title: The Last Interview on the List
名單上的最後一位面試者
paras: Elise Mendez handled {{recruitment|recruitment}} for a small shipping company, and for two months she had been trying to fill a {{vacancy|vacancy}} on the dispatch team. On Tuesday afternoon she met the last {{applicant|applicant}} on her list, a quiet man named Victor Lane.
艾莉絲．門德斯替一家小型貨運公司負責招募，兩個月來一直想補上調度組的一個職缺。週二下午，她見了名單上的最後一位應徵者，一個安靜的男人，名叫維克多．連恩。

The form asked for his {{occupation|occupation}}, and he had written "senior dispatcher" in the box. The opening, however, was a {{junior|junior}} position with a modest salary. "Frankly, I'm worried you'll be bored," Elise said. Victor shrugged. "My old company closed in March. I'd rather start lower than not work at all."
表格上要他填職業，他在欄位裡寫的是「資深調度員」。然而這個缺是資淺職位，薪水不高。「老實說，我擔心你會覺得無聊。」艾莉絲說。維克多聳聳肩：「我之前的公司三月倒閉了。我寧可從低一點的職位做起，也不想沒工作。」

Elise was still {{reluctant|reluctant}} to say yes. Overqualified people often leave a job like this within six months. Then Victor asked something she rarely heard from a {{prospective|prospective}} employee, someone who did not even have the job yet. "Who would train me? I'd like to learn your routes first, not change them." That settled it for her.
艾莉絲還是不太願意馬上點頭，因為像這樣的工作，資歷過高的人常常做不到半年就走了。接著維克多問了一個問題，是她很少從還沒錄取的未來員工口中聽到的：「請問誰會帶我？我想先把你們的路線學起來，而不是急著去改它。」這讓她下了決心。
On Thursday she {{formally|formally}} offered him the job by email. His {{acceptance|acceptance}} came back twenty minutes later, with one short line underneath: "When do I start?"
週四，她用電子郵件正式向他提出聘用。二十分鐘後，他接受的回信就來了，底下只有短短一行：「我什麼時候開始上班？」
